html:
Nicaragua is the largest country of Central America, between Honduras and Costa Rica, with great lakes and a long Caribbean coast. It has been a separate republic since 1838.

Its Spanish colonial towns, liberal León and conservative Granada, fought each other for decades after independence. The Caribbean side, the Mosquito Coast, was a British protectorate over the Miskito people for much of the 1800s and was only fully joined to Nicaragua in 1894. Its lakes made it a favoured route between the oceans:

  • During the California gold rush, travellers crossed Nicaragua by boat and coach.
  • In 1856 the American adventurer William Walker made himself president, until Central American armies drove him out.
  • A Nicaraguan canal was long planned, but the United States chose Panama instead.

US Marines occupied the country from 1912 to 1933. Augusto César Sandino fought them as a guerrilla leader and was murdered in 1934 on the orders of Anastasio Somoza. The Somoza family then ruled for over forty years. After an earthquake destroyed Managua in 1972 and aid money vanished, opposition grew.

The Sandinistas, named after Sandino, overthrew the last Somoza in 1979. The United States backed the Contras in a long war against them. Violeta Chamorro beat the Sandinistas in the 1990 election. The Sandinista leader Daniel Ortega returned to power in 2007 and has ruled since in an increasingly authoritarian way.
sum: Nicaragua is the largest country of Central America, between Honduras and Costa Rica, with great lakes and a long Caribbean coast. It has been a separate republic since 1838.
